questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Offered classes at the university and closeness to my home country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found there to be way way too many things that needed to be documented in certain ways and a lot of stress in this regard both before, during and after my exchange. Had I known that it would be so hectic and problematic, then I would have waited and not done it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: 6/10. We were told to always use the university website, but as it was filled with information and consisted of 4 different platforms, it was quite confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting at the faculty, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult, which for sure also added to my initial stress about the exchange. I was told that the university would not be able to guarantee any kind of assistance and was therefore highly encouraged to find my own housing if I wanted to be sure that I could fulfill my exchange. I later experienced that several students did in fact get housing through the university, so I wish they'd been a bit more forthcoming in this regard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I had the absolute best time! Only problem was the incredibly high rent. 
Other than that I lived in a great place with absolute great people. My housing is for sure my main source for finding friends and overall socializing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of confusion because the host university was changing their system for course registration just as I arrived, which meant that no one really knew what exactly to do. I found the process to not correspond with the constant deadlines that were put in place by my own university, who wished for me to fill out the OLA. As I needed the courses for this process I felt like I was put in a tough spot then.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly do not remember the initial registration, but only the course registration after I received my spot. It was a mix of two different platforms and the course catalogue. Trying to find the classes that I already get 'pre-acceptance' for at my university and also being mindful of all the different schedules and of course hoping for availability.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a number that I called once to get assistance, as the schedules were changed for several classes so I had to re-apply for new ones.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get my first priority unfortunately, but thankfully I found that the faculty offered a lot of interesting classes so I found others that were interesting but did not necessarily have anything to do with my major.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would let them know that they will be okay and that even though the deadlines might seem like non-negotiable, you can only do so much and sometimes things are just out of your hands.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really good classes and professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were harder in the sense that I took classes outside of my major, but I also found it fairly easy to adapt. I had to get used to the amount of hand-ins, projects etc. that were required for even small 6 credit classes, as this was very different from what I am used to, where usually we work on one or two bigger project per class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I prefer the style of teaching at UCPH, simply because I find my teachers there to be quite extraordinary. But I did really enjoy the many different teaching styles that I encountered at UVA.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Urban multilingualism 1, Urban multilingualism 2, Ethics and the good life, Feminism and philosophy & Philosophy of gender, race and intersectionality

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all three philosophy classes. The course litteratur was really interesting and the class dynamics were interestering, particularly in the class: Philosophy of gender, race and intersectionality

questions.answer: I actually only saw these kind of opportunities through the ESN community

questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to museums, going to house/techno parties and using the opportunity to visit both other cities in the Netherlands such as The Hague and also nearby cities such as Brussels and maybe Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me as I think the dutch are very similar to the danish. It was cool to meet a lot of other exchange students that were different from both the danish and the dutch.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socialize during classes and maybe accept that you'll be more likely to hang out with other exchange students if you are only there for one semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I cannot really think of anything particularly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The arts and music scene.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will be part of an incredibly international environment, with UVA having 40% international students. Be prepared to get 'checked' (by testing and mandatory participation) a great deal more than in DK and enjoy living in a really beautiful city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything administrative can take a bit of time, even though everyone really tries to help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting great people and having the knowledge that I did it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Administrative stuff and stress in that regard

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
